subject: Civil Engineering
title: Earth Pressure Balance TBMs
description: A quick, practical guide to Earth Pressure Balance TBMs.

hook.text: In soft, wet ground, the tunnel face can collapse or flood instantly. EPB machines prevent both.

buildup.text: An EPB TBM keeps excavated soil in a sealed chamber behind the cutterhead.

discovery.text: The pressurized soil balances groundwater and earth pressure — holding the face stable.

twist.text: A screw conveyor extracts soil slowly — controlling pressure as material exits the chamber.

climax.text: Crossrail's EPB machines tunneled under London — through clay, gravel, and sand safely.

punchline.text: Use the excavated soil itself to hold the ground open. Elegant engineering.

quiz.question: How does an EPB TBM prevent face collapse in soft ground?
options: It freezes the ground ahead of the cutterhead to stabilize it
Excavated soil is kept pressurized in a sealed chamber to balance earth and water pressure
It injects concrete into the ground before cutting through it
